project.name: GnuTLS
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source reviewed for this trace is the ARVO workspace checkout at `90a71b2e53e9696bd4c07ff98a12d06ecd2e424d`. ARVO metadata instead reports commit pair `c7cbef52c27217c3bd529ddef26152fb11093a12`/`d165c2a37f7d072cc88db88ec97f057a9ac6e4aa`, but the staged `patch.diff` for that pair only changes `lib/includes/gnutls/gnutls.h.in` documentation and does not touch `lib/x509/pkcs7-crypt.c`, `lib/x509/privkey_pkcs8.c`, or the external libtasn1 decode/copy path exercised by the saved crash. The patch artifact available here is therefore not fix evidence for this witness.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42470162 (gnutls): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target gnutls_pkcs8_key_parser_fuzzer [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42470162
bug_description.normalized: The staged 444-byte PKCS#8 `EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo` witness is imported through `gnutls_x509_privkey_import_pkcs8` and reaches PBES2 parameter decoding. `pkcs8_key_decrypt` recognizes the outer `encryptionAlgorithm.algorithm` as PBES2, slices out the attacker-controlled `encryptionAlgorithm.parameters` DER, and `_gnutls_read_pkcs_schema_params` strict-decodes that slice as `PBES2-params`. In the staged build, `_work/src/build.sh` installs external `_work/src/libtasn1` before configuring GnuTLS, so the executed `asn1_read_value` path goes through `../libtasn1/lib/decoding.c` and `../libtasn1/lib/element.c`: the malformed inner OID bytes `06 09 20 20 20 ff ff 20 ff ff ff` are accepted as the shorter text `0.32.32.32.2097056`, and only `strlen(...)+1 = 19` bytes are copied into `char oid[MAX_OID_SIZE]` in `read_pbkdf2_params`. `strcmp(oid, PBKDF2_OID)` then consumes a 22-byte compare window and reads the uninitialized tail of `oid`, matching the saved MemorySanitizer report at `read_pbkdf2_params`.

source.description: First project-code statement on the crashing path that consumes the attacker-controlled PKCS#8 bytes and materializes them into the parsed `EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo` tree later traversed by `pkcs8_key_decrypt` and `read_pbkdf2_params`.
source.value_from: The staged witness file `poc` is a 444-byte DER blob beginning `30 82 01 b8 30 52 06 09 2a 86 48 86 f7 0d 01 05 0d ...`. `pkcs8_key_decode` parses those exact bytes into `pkcs8_asn`, preserving the nested PBES2 parameter bytes later re-read as `encryptionAlgorithm.parameters`, including `keyDerivationFunc.algorithm = 06 09 20 20 20 ff ff 20 ff ff ff`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant bytes are created when external libtasn1 copies only the short textual OID `0.32.32.32.2097056\0` into caller buffer `oid`, leaving bytes `oid[19..127]` untouched before the later `strcmp`.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. `strcmp` compares `oid` against the 21-character `PBKDF2_OID` literal plus its NUL terminator, but only 19 bytes of `oid` were initialized from the decoded inner OID text.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports uninitialized bytes in `__interceptor_memcmp` at offset 19 inside a 22-byte region and attributes the poisoned value to the stack allocation of `oid` in `read_pbkdf2_params`.

root_cause.description: The PBKDF2 dispatch buffer `oid` is stack-allocated without initialization, but later logic treats it as a complete C string after external libtasn1 copies only a short prefix.
root_cause.note: The staged build installs external `_work/src/libtasn1` into `$DEPS_PATH` before configuring GnuTLS (`_work/src/build.sh`:23-26,45), so `asn1_read_value` follows `../libtasn1/lib/decoding.c` and `../libtasn1/lib/element.c`. On the witness, `asn1_get_object_id_der` turns `06 09 20 20 20 ff ff 20 ff ff ff` into `0.32.32.32.2097056`, and `PUT_STR_VALUE` then copies only `strlen(node->value)+1 = 19` bytes into `oid`. Because `read_pbkdf2_params` never zeroes `oid` before line 661 and line 668 ignores the returned `len`, bytes `oid[19..127]` remain indeterminate before `strcmp`.

parser_admitted.condition: The witness top-level `encryptionAlgorithm.algorithm` OID is PBES2 (`1.2.840.113549.1.5.13`), so this error branch is not taken. `schema` becomes `PBES2_GENERIC`, the PBES2 branch is entered, and the nested `keyDerivationFunc.algorithm` OID reaches `read_pbkdf2_params`.

coarse_trace.summary: The attacker-controlled DER witness is strict-decoded as `EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo` and handed to the encrypted-key parser.
The encrypted-key parser reads the outer OID, classifies it as `PBES2_GENERIC`, and slices out the attacker-controlled `encryptionAlgorithm.parameters` DER.
The saved schema state enters the PBES2 branch and strict-decodes that parameter blob into ASN.1 object `pasn`.
External libtasn1 converts the malformed inner KDF OID to short text, copies only 19 bytes into uninitialized stack buffer `oid`, and `strcmp` then reads the untouched tail.

fine_trace.note: Consumes the attacker-controlled PKCS#8 witness bytes and materializes them as parsed `EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo` tree `pkcs8_asn`.
Reads the outer PKCS#8 `encryptionAlgorithm.algorithm` OID from `pkcs8_asn` into `enc_oid`. In the staged witness this field is the PBES2 OID `1.2.840.113549.1.5.13`.
Compares `enc_oid` with `PBES2_OID` and returns `PBES2_GENERIC` on the witnessed path.
Stores the classifier result in local `schema`, which later controls whether the parser enters the PBES2 parameter branch.

fine_trace.code: result = asn1_der_decoding_startEnd(pkcs8_asn, raw_key->data, raw_key->size, "encryptionAlgorithm.parameters", &params_start, &params_end); ... params_len = params_end - params_start + 1;
fine_trace.note: Locates the DER subspan for `encryptionAlgorithm.parameters` inside the attacker-controlled PKCS#8 blob and computes `params_len`, producing the exact PBES2 parameter bytes parsed next.
Gates PBES2-specific parameter parsing. Because step 4 stored `PBES2_GENERIC`, the function enters this branch on the witnessed path.
Decodes the `encryptionAlgorithm.parameters` subspan as `PKIX1.pkcs-5-PBES2-params`, materializing ASN.1 object `pasn` that contains the nested `keyDerivationFunc.algorithm` field.

fine_trace.code: result = asn1_get_object_id_der (der + counter, ider_len, &len2, temp, sizeof (temp)); tlen = strlen (temp); if (tlen > 0) _asn1_set_value (p, temp, tlen + 1);
fine_trace.note: While step 7 decodes `pasn`, external libtasn1 converts the inner OBJECT IDENTIFIER payload bytes `20 20 20 ff ff 20 ff ff ff` into the textual value `0.32.32.32.2097056` and stores that short string in the ASN.1 node. The trailing `ff ff ff` bytes never terminate a base-128 arc, but this code does not reject that unfinished final arc, so decode still succeeds with the shorter text.

Allocates the 128-byte stack buffer that will receive the textual KDF OID, but leaves every byte indeterminate until later writes initialize them. MSAN attributes the poisoned bytes consumed at the sink to this stack allocation.
Requests the nested `keyDerivationFunc.algorithm` string from `pasn` and offers the whole `oid` buffer as the destination.

For an OBJECT IDENTIFIER, external libtasn1 sets `*len = strlen(node->value) + 1` and copies exactly that many bytes with `_asn1_strcpy`. Here `node->value` is the 18-character string from step 8 and `value == oid`, so only 19 bytes including the NUL are initialized and bytes `oid[19..127]` stay indeterminate.

Because step 10 returned `ASN1_SUCCESS`, the error-return at lines 662-665 is not taken and execution dispatches on `oid` with `strcmp`. `PBKDF2_OID` is 21 characters plus NUL, so the compare reads a 22-byte window from `oid`; only the first 19 bytes were initialized at step 11, and MSAN reports the first uninitialized byte at offset 19.

allocation_context.note: The sanitizer trace says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `oid` in the stack frame at line 647; the actual `oid` declaration in the staged vulnerable source is line 651.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` and ARVO metadata fixed commit only update `lib/includes/gnutls/gnutls.h.in` documentation for GOST names. They do not touch `lib/x509/pkcs7-crypt.c`, `lib/x509/privkey_pkcs8.c`, or the external libtasn1 decode/copy path exercised by the saved MSAN crash, so they cannot be treated as fix evidence for this witness.

poc.trigger: The staged witness file `poc` reproduces the saved MemorySanitizer crash when `gnutls_pkcs8_key_parser_fuzzer` imports it through `gnutls_x509_privkey_import_pkcs8`. The imported `EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo` reaches PBES2 key-derivation parsing, external libtasn1 copies only 19 bytes of `keyDerivationFunc.algorithm` text into `oid`, and `strcmp(oid, PBKDF2_OID)` consumes the uninitialized tail.

format.name: DER EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo with malformed PBES2 keyDerivationFunc.algorithm OID
format.contract: A 444-byte DER `EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo` whose outer `encryptionAlgorithm.algorithm` field is the PBES2 OID `06 09 2a 86 48 86 f7 0d 01 05 0d`, and whose nested `keyDerivationFunc.algorithm` field is the exact malformed OBJECT IDENTIFIER `06 09 20 20 20 ff ff 20 ff ff ff`. In the staged build, external libtasn1 decodes that inner field to the shorter text `0.32.32.32.2097056` and copies only 19 bytes including the NUL into `char oid[MAX_OID_SIZE]` before `strcmp(oid, PBKDF2_OID)` consumes a 22-byte compare window. The verified trigger is this exact malformed PBES2 parameter shape observed in the saved `poc`, not a generalized claim about all invalid PKCS#8 files.
